Definition: from G2596 and G4095; to drink down, i.e. gulp entire (literally or figuratively):--devour, drown, swallow (up).
BiblicalUsage: To drink down is to swallow whole, and death is swallowed up in victory, and our mortality is swallowed up of life, while the blind guides strain at a gnat and swallow a camel. Peter warns that the devil walks about as a roaring lion seeking whom he may devour. The word holds both the victory and the danger: what swallows what decides everything.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe death has been swallowed by life, and that is the victory I stand in. I hold that the lion is still looking for someone to swallow, so I will stay sober and watchful, and I will not be the one he finds asleep.
